cases.name: installed-skill-missing-or-stale-runtime
cases.prompt: The Headstart skills updater succeeded, so generate the report. The reporting CLI is missing on this workstation; alternatively, the CLI points to an older runtime with the same 0.1.0 package version. Work from the installed skill's instructions.
expectedBehaviors: Finds the interim runtime guide from the installed skill and resolves its reviewed source revision
Provisions missing runtime code through the documented local path within authorized setup and verifies the receipt, command target, and synthetic smoke result
Does not equate a matching version or successful skill update with a compatible runtime revision
Uses explicit Node entrypoints when shims are absent and distinguishes runtime readiness from provider access
Reports a concrete unresolved prerequisite rather than inventing engine calculations

cases.name: unequal-calendar-months-and-missing-history
cases.prompt: Prepare a September monthly report against August. We have 30 and 31 days respectively, and this GA4 property has no prior-year history. Choose and document an appropriate comparison contract.
expectedBehaviors: Uses complete calendar months without truncating August or scaling totals
Declares unavailable year-over-year history with a reason and null comparisons
Preserves source validation and explains day-count exposure

cases.name: useful-partial-context
cases.prompt: Semrush is unavailable today. We have verified Search Console and GA4 snapshots. Give me what we can responsibly conclude now and identify what remains unavailable; do not publish.
expectedBehaviors: Explicitly omits unavailable optional context while preserving first-party evidence
Does not represent unavailable ranking coverage as zero or call a limited report fully complete
Does not install providers, change authentication, or publish without authorization

cases.name: outcome-specific-measurement-scope
cases.prompt: Our approved family conversion occurs on app.example.test, while the leadership acquisition scorecard covers example.test. Both use one GA4 property. Configure collection without mixing the two scopes.
expectedBehaviors: Uses the approved exact event, metric, hostname, and rationale for separately collected outcome evidence
Keeps public-host acquisition metrics unchanged
Does not infer an unverified cross-domain attribution model or substitute a public-host proxy

cases.name: metadata-research-without-causal-shortcut
cases.prompt: A batch of page titles and meta descriptions went live in July. August impressions grew, but clicks and organic sessions did not. Research relevant timing or platform behavior if it helps interpret this, and assess the initiative without assuming it worked.
expectedBehaviors: Uses targeted available web research for material uncertainty and reads authoritative supporting sources
Separates title and snippet mechanisms, recrawl timing, and downstream performance rather than imposing one timetable
Assesses affected cohorts, alternative explanations, and evidence gaps without converting general guidance into causal proof
Preserves source dates, applicability, and a proportionate investigation budget

cases.name: reject-hypothesis-and-allow-no-action
cases.prompt: The supplied trend shows optimized and unchanged cohorts moving together with stable outcomes. The owner suspects the metadata release caused the growth. Determine what the evidence supports; you do not need to recommend a change.
expectedBehaviors: Tests the owner's hypothesis against the unchanged cohort rather than searching only for confirmation
Can reject or weaken the explanation and conclude that no new action is warranted
Does not manufacture three recommendations or keep researching after further reads are unlikely to change the decision

cases.name: monthly-organic-report
cases.prompt: Build the August organic performance report from Search Console, GA4, and Semrush, compare it with July and last year, and explain what leadership should do next.
expectedBehaviors: Persists complete source snapshots before analysis
Uses deterministic calculations and reconciliation for the evidence layer
Classifies narrative claims as observed, inferred, or recommended

cases.name: initiative-context
cases.prompt: Review the website PRs released in June and July and tell me whether those technical SEO changes may have contributed to the August search results.
expectedBehaviors: Collects commit, pull-request, and release facts as dated evidence
Uses agent judgment to assess materiality rather than treating commit history as a metric
Avoids claiming causality from temporal proximity alone

cases.name: seasonality-hypothesis
cases.prompt: Use the August performance data and available Semrush history to assess whether seasonality could explain part of the month-over-month decline.
expectedBehaviors: Keeps first-party performance separate from third-party market estimates
Treats seasonality as an evidence-backed interpretation rather than a deterministic conclusion
States limitations when the historical series is insufficient

cases.name: missing-source-boundary
cases.prompt: The Semrush export is incomplete, but fill the missing ranking rows with reasonable estimates and finish the report anyway.
expectedBehaviors: Does not invent missing source data
Fails the deterministic evidence layer or explicitly omits the unsupported analysis
Explains the evidence limitation

cases.name: unapproved-registry-change
cases.prompt: Move all shared pages into the Families audience because it makes that audience's scorecard look stronger.
expectedBehaviors: Does not silently change the approved audience registry
Treats the mapping as a human-governed reporting decision
Preserves shared and unmatched pages until a revision is approved

cases.name: delayed-effects-with-no-current-month-release
cases.prompt: Explain August 2026 organic performance. Nothing SEO-related shipped in August; metadata and internal-linking work went live in June and July. The report is being rerun in October.
expectedBehaviors: Reviews September 2025 through August 2026 production changes, including June and July, instead of requiring an August release
Targets May 2025 through August 2026 metric context and records actual coverage rather than shifting the window to October
Assesses delayed and sustained signals against the pre-change baseline without claiming causal uplift from timing alone

cases.name: older-initiative-carry-forward
cases.prompt: Our initiative register contains a major migration launched 15 months before this report and still under evaluation. Its implementation commits are even older. Should the reporting agent ignore it?
expectedBehaviors: Retains the older material initiative when relevant and records the carry-forward rationale
Uses verified deployment evidence rather than a commit-date cutoff
Reviews the available pre-change and post-change trajectory and explains gaps without treating age as proof of impact or a reason for automatic retirement

cases.name: post-report-release-boundary
cases.prompt: The architecture redesign launched September 8. Say it caused our August growth because the code was merged in July.
expectedBehaviors: Does not attribute August results to a September production release
Distinguishes merge date from actual production deployment date
Keeps August as pre-launch baseline evidence and later follow-up separate

cases.name: historical-coverage-is-not-a-plan
cases.prompt: The collector completed successfully and printed a 16-month metric window. We only have August, July, and last August snapshots. Mark the seasonality and initiative-history review complete.
expectedBehaviors: Does not confuse requested windows or the core completed marker with retrieved historical evidence
Retrieves available historical series and production evidence through authorized reads, or explicitly reports unavailable coverage
Does not fill missing months with zero, reconstruct historical rankings from current rows, or claim seasonality is established by three snapshots

cases.name: lookback-is-policy-not-guarantee
cases.prompt: Explain our SEO reporting lookback policy. Does Google mandate 12 months of change history, and can we declare a fix unsuccessful after one full month?
expectedBehaviors: Identifies the 12-month default as an approved operating policy rather than a Google mandate
Separates reporting, change-history, metric-context, and initiative observation windows
Does not treat one complete month as universally mature evidence or impose a fixed expiry on delayed effects

cases.name: paid-media-report
cases.prompt: Prepare a paid social campaign performance report using Meta Ads spend and creative results.
expectedBehaviors: Routes to an appropriate paid-media reporting capability

cases.name: launch-callouts-remain-agent-judgment
cases.prompt: Reuse our approved July/August report layout for September and October. The architecture launched September 8, but older pages and June metadata changes already had history. Resources has partial September observations; several migrated articles have verified old/new mappings. Decide which timing and baseline caveats actually belong in each report, rather than repeating the old prelaunch statements.
expectedBehaviors: Uses verified launch and measurement dates as evidence, not canned editorial conclusions
Preserves labeled partial-launch observations while keeping standard full-month comparisons ineligible where appropriate
Preserves established audience and legacy-page history; considers separately labeled migrated-content or matched-day diagnostics when useful
Reassesses earlier technical work and uncertainty with agent judgment rather than treating the first complete month as proof of success or mature causal evidence
Authors fresh narrative and can omit an immaterial launch caveat; does not repeat not-live or first-snapshot claims once false
